The retained 2.91% is a deliberate, bounded toehold, not an unspecified observation position: a 10% adverse move costs ~$291 (0.29% of total equity) while a 10% rebound contributes the same, preserving participation in a franchise that printed +16.4% revenue, 50.06% gross margin, +28.7% EPS and $110.2B of nine-month FCF. final.investment_thesis:
The decision is Hold with the position retained, because the two halves of the evidence genuinely offset — this is not conflict-as-excuse, it is the correct read after weighing. The bull side is concrete and unrefuted: Q3 FY26 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, EPS +28.7% to $2.02, nine-month free cash flow $110.2B, ~$62.2B net cash, and price still 7.9% above a rising 200 SMA at 280.09 with the 50/200 spread ~29.4 points. The bear side is equally concrete and near-term decisive: price 302.25 sits below the 10 EMA (311.35), the 50 SMA (309.48), the VWMA (317.19) and the Bollinger mid (321.22); the 50 SMA has just rolled over; a 10/50 death cross is close; MACD is below zero at -1.735 with the histogram re-widening; RSI is 40.22 and not oversold; and the low-volume bounce failed into 309.5-317.2 overhead supply. That combination blocks adding at 302.25 — and it is the same configuration that burned the 2026-08-05 Overweight (-3.1% alpha) by entering before its own 311.80/>65M gate, and the 2026-08-03 Overweight (-0.3%) by buying mid-chop. But it does not justify liquidating a 2.91% position: the prior Underweight lessons (2026-07-31, -2.1%) show that selling inside an intact primary trend without a printed trigger bleeds alpha, and the average cost of $309.89 is explicitly not a reason to hold — only the marginal risk/reward of total exposure is.

Sizing, weighed against total account equity. At 302.25, 9.6227 shares are worth ~$2,908 (2.91% of ~$99,814) against ~$96,906 cash (97.1%). Downside: a 10% decline costs ~$291 (0.29% of equity), a 20% decline ~$582 (0.58%); only a break of the 200 SMA at 280.09 would mark a primary-trend break worth a full exit review. Upside forgone at zero: a 10% rebound contributes the same ~$291 (0.29%), and a decisive move toward the 2026 highs would leave 97.1% of equity in zero-interest cash. The two magnitudes are roughly symmetric, which is precisely why neither the aggressive analyst's push to 6-10% nor a full liquidation wins. The 6-10% case is rejected because $599-$998 of exposure per 10% move would be added with every near-term signal negative and before the 311.4/317.2 volume-confirmation gates; the 0% case is rejected because it forgoes ~$291 of plausible upside and crystallizes a -$73.5 loss plus fees to shave a 0.29% risk line — uneconomic churn. The retained 2.91% earns its place as a low-cost, bounded claim on the top-of-cycle margin and FCF profile; it does not earn a larger one until the tape confirms.

Where the analysts split and how I resolved it: the aggressive analyst is right that 97.1% zero-interest cash is a real, deterministic opportunity cost and that the 2.91% should not be dismissed as a passive 'observation position' — but that argument cuts only to preserving the position, not to pre-empting confirmation by adding. The conservative analyst is right to cap exposure until 311.4/317.2 are reclaimed on volume, but wrong to characterize the holding as valueless; at 0.29% of equity per 10% move it is a functional, revocable participation stake. The neutral analyst's synthesis — keep, cap, quantify both tails — is the surviving framework, and all three converge on keep_shares with no daily rebalance at 10-bps round-trip cost.

What would change this. Upside: a daily close above 311.4 (10 EMA), ideally above 317.2 (VWMA), on volume above ~55M shares justifies a modest add toward 5-6%; a close above 321.2 (Bollinger mid) holding the 322-324 confluence would justify scaling further. Downside: a decisive close below 300.00 on >55M shares moves toward trimming, and a close below 280.09 (200 SMA) is a primary-trend break requiring full exit review. A gross-margin print below 47-48% at the next report, or guidance implying two consecutive sub-47% quarters, would downgrade toward Underweight regardless of the tape. These are narrative conditions only, not implemented stops or conditional orders, and they are explicitly separated from today's keep_shares execution.

Stated gaps, not papered over: the news sample covers only a fraction of the window with little full text; no entry price is provided for the next open (which is unknown and where the 10-bps fee would apply); and no valuation multiples, consensus forward estimates, options chain or implied move are in the record — so the exposure decision rests on the supplied technical and fundamental data and the account arithmetic, not on a valuation-derived target.
